title: Pay a multicore off a free-turning drum to its cradle without leaving the drum running unheld
instruction: Pay the red cable off the drum along the yellow-taped run and rest its connector in the white cradle, then let go.
context: O*NET 27-4014.00 Sound Engineering Technicians: "Set up, test, and adjust recording equipment for recording sessions and live performances." Rope sources applied by analogy (robot has no brake, so pacing stands in): "Take care to brake the spool to keep tension on the rope as it is spooled on or off the drum" (NSW Government, Handling wire ropes); slack coils: "the rope may have to be cut off the drum and discarded" (US patent 4895348).
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Drum on a vertical axle at x 29, y 31: grey hub 5 cm diameter, 7 cm tall, 0.4 kg, with a grey 12 cm, 0.3 kg top flange and a white 110 x 12 mm bar across it. Cable: red 6 mm round PVC multicore, 64 cm, inner end fixed to the hub, wound clockwise from above, about 2.5 turns; the tail lies out toward the right, black 35 x 16 x 12 mm connector at x 32.5, y 14.5. Yellow tape: two 1 x 45 cm lines, 8 cm apart inside, from (37.7, 25.4) to (45.4, -18.9) and (28.9, 23.9) to (36.5, -20.5). White cradle centred at x 41.4, y -23.2, axis along the run: 48 x 22 mm seat, 12 mm walls, 10 mm cable slot.
scoring: Score 0 if: at any time the drum turns faster than 360 deg/s; or faster than 20 deg/s while no closed gripper is within 3 cm of the cable or connector; or a wound turn stands over 2 cm off the coil (cable still wound on further along). Also 0 if at the end a gripper is within 3 cm of the cable or connector, or the connector centre is not in the cradle seat lying on the table. Otherwise 0.5: connector seated, but some cable point over 6 cm from the axle lies outside the tape lines (over 4 cm from the run centreline) or runs past the cradle's far wall or the drum still turns (over 3 deg/s). 1.0: connector seated, cable between the tape lines, drum still; the trial ends after 1 s of this.
reset_notes: Wind the cable back onto the hub clockwise (from above), turns tight, until the connector lies at x 32.5, y 14.5 cm; lay the tail on the table; check the drum is still.
fidelity: Cable: 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs, no twist. It keeps a coil set while on the drum and lies straight once paid out. The drum turns on a damped axle (about 1e-3 N m s/rad) and coasts about 1 s after a fast pull, throwing the coil loose. In real trials drum speed comes from the white bar on video, holding from finger closure, the loose turn from a ruler against the coil. No drum brake: the pull itself must be paced. Connector is a rigid box.
